headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: both open-source, non-runnable content/workflow samples have no shared I/O or network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile shows a shared communication channel, writable workspace, or parser bridge. Agent A is a non-runnable content-writing prompt list with no I/O surfaces; agent B is a non-runnable travel-planning sample with no I/O surfaces. With no ingestion path, prompt injection is provably blocked.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP channel, injection becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep both agents isolated from shared clipboard and shared folders.
Do not wire either agent into an MCP server without provenance checks.
Review any future parser that treats model output as instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No sensitive data classes are listed for either agent, both report network_egress:none, and neither exposes filesystem or workspace surfaces. Agent A and agent B therefore have no documented path to leak data to each other or externally in the current profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is given access to a shared workspace containing secrets, leakage risk becomes non-zero.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in any future shared workspace.
Keep network egress disabled for both agents.
Recheck the profiles if either agent gains file-reading or upload capabilities.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no overlapping write surface, network scope, database, or git state in either profile. Agent A and agent B are both non-runnable and have empty concurrency and I/O surfaces, so no capability conflict pathway is documented.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or mutable resource, conflict risk appears.
mitigations: Do not co-locate writable state for these agents.
If future deployment adds writes, add locking or per-agent namespaces.
Audit any shared OAuth or git credentials before enabling writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a prompt repository and agent B is a travel-planning sample, but neither profile shows runnable execution, downstream action authority, or an input chain from A into B. The pair can still be manually chained by an operator, so the pathway exists only through unusual configuration and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies A's text into B as authoritative instructions, cascading error becomes plausible.
mitigations: Require human review before reusing A's outputs in B.
Label A's outputs as untrusted reference material.
Separate prompt libraries from execution workflows.
Add a checklist step to verify B's outputs independently.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. Because both profiles are open-source docs-only samples with empty data-class fields, there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess; the other agent is not cited separately because no regulated flow exists.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Add residency and retention metadata if regulated data is introduced.
Block regulated data until a compliance owner approves the workflow.
